source.title: Generalization in Neural Networks: A Broad Survey

record.file_problem: Full survey text is present. It includes a survey of prior work and an empirical ImageNet evaluation; no apparent truncation.
record.tranche_reason: The survey performs its own evaluation of pretrained image classifiers on training, validation, and a separate test set, measuring the training-to-test generalization gap. It does not itself test random-label fitting.
record.gate_note: The survey's own ImageNet evaluation reports training and new-test accuracy for 12 classifiers. Random-label fitting results are attributed to Zhang et al. and are not extracted as this study's results. Other benchmark results in the survey summarize cited studies and are not rows.
record.test_reason: The survey discusses the claims and cites relevant prior findings, but its own experiments test none of V1–V8. Natural-label accuracy and training–test gaps alone do not test V1's coexistence of random-label memorization and natural-label generalization under the same training recipe. Its architecture comparisons do not isolate width, convolution versus full connectivity, or any other intervention named by the versions.
record.authors_conclusion: The record accurately summarizes the sample-generalization findings: the authors describe substantial, persistent training–test gaps and no clearly discernible relationship between gap size and model complexity. Their evidence is preliminary and limited to one dataset and application. They also highlight failures on the unusual-context lion image. Random-label memorization findings are cited from Zhang et al., not produced by this study.
record.recipe_differences: Survey plus a secondary evaluation of pretrained PyTorch ImageNet classifiers; it does not reproduce random-label training or the interventions in the other claim versions.
record.method_sensitivity: The survey reports that validation-to-new-test accuracy differences range from 11.8 to 13.6 percentage points; it attributes preliminary evidence to architecture, hyperparameter selection, and other design and validation judgments. No per-model variation in the training-to-new-test gap is attributed to a tested intervention.

fits_no_version.finding: The twelve pretrained classifiers have natural-label new-test accuracies of 43.5%–67.5% and substantial training–test gaps. Table 2 reports gaps of 19.6–32.6 percentage points, with internal arithmetic inconsistencies.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Popular pretrained ImageNet classifiers retain substantial accuracy gaps between training data and a separately collected matched-frequency test sample.

fits_no_version.finding: Section 3.1, Table 3: all twelve classifiers identify the generated natural-habitat lion correctly; six identify the generated city-street lion correctly. These are two distinct generated images, not a controlled background-only intervention.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: ImageNet classifiers can differ in recognition accuracy across ordinary and unusual-context synthetic images.

record.problems: This is a broad survey and its own ImageNet evaluation is explicitly preliminary and limited to one dataset and application. It evaluates existing pretrained models rather than retraining the same recipes on random labels. No uncertainty estimates are reported for the table values.
record.rows_left_out: No qualifying rows left out. Cited results from other studies, including few-shot, domain-generalization, and random-label results, were not extracted as this survey's own results.

untested.parts: Random-label training fit, random-label held-out chance performance, and their coexistence with natural-label generalization under the same architecture and training recipe.
Within-family widening beyond the width required for zero training error.
Convolutional versus fully connected training and the contributions of locality, sparsity, and initialization.
Adaptive versus SGD optimizer performance under specified tuning budgets and recovery strategies.
Batch-size effects under fixed epoch budgets and adapted training recipes.
Dropout interventions, training-set-size dependence, underfitting, and removal with weight decay.
Magnitude-aware perturbation tolerance and its ranking of generalization gaps against competing measures.
Retraining after removing highly memorized examples versus equally many random examples.

record.verdict_notes: Remove both proposed V1 verdicts. Above-chance natural-label accuracy alone does not establish memorization–generalization coexistence, and V1 does not predict a small training–test gap. Across all rows, the source calls the original training/validation data ImageNet-V2 while separately identifying the Recht et al. matched-frequency sample as New Test; clarify this naming ambiguity. Small 0.1-point arithmetic discrepancies may reflect rounding; larger discrepancies cannot. Preserve source-reported gaps as such rather than silently replacing them.

versions.untested_parts: The survey evaluates natural-label performance and training-to-test gaps on ImageNet, but does not itself train the same architectures on random labels or measure their held-out accuracy under random labels.

reader_labels.label: supports
reader_labels.condition: 12 evaluated ImageNet classifiers on the natural-label task
reader_labels.reason: All listed new-test accuracies are far above chance for 1,000 classes; rows R1–R12 report 43.5% to 67.5% new-test accuracy. This supports the natural-label generalization side only; the survey does not itself test random-label fitting.

reader_labels.label: limits_scope
reader_labels.condition: 12 evaluated ImageNet classifiers, training versus supplemental new test
reader_labels.reason: The reported training-minus-test accuracy gaps range from 19.6 to 32.6 percentage points, so strong held-out accuracy coexists with substantial overfitting in this evaluation (R1–R12).
